channel.title: Experimental Newsroom
channel.description: Careful observation, evidence and constructive criticism from Experimental Newsroom.

item.title: En god eier kan også bli en mektig eier
item.description: Amediastiftelsen har avtalt å kjøpe Aschehoug. Sparebankstiftelsen DNB bekrefter et nytt lån til kjøpet, samtidig som styret der velger Amediastiftelsens styre. Langsiktighet er begrunnelsen for finansieringen. Hvordan fordeles ansvar og beslutningsmakt når avisutgivelse og forlagsvirksomhet får samme eier?

item.title: England revisits motorway charging after a pilot awarded no grants
item.description: After every applicant withdrew from a grid-upgrade pilot, England proposed a different funding arrangement. Its value will depend on whether the new connections help drivers find charging they can use and afford.

item.title: What can a bank know about whether care happened?
item.description: A federal analysis follows $17.5 billion in activity that financial institutions considered suspicious. Understanding what happened to the money still requires evidence about the care behind the payments.

item.title: Ask before you buy
item.description: Before deciding what to buy for its care services, Hsinchu County asked for knowledge. Its notices show how early questions can give more people a part in shaping the eventual service.

item.title: Before the System Is Locked In
item.description: In the 1970s, Norwegian unions and researchers explored how workers could help shape computer systems. Their experience speaks to today's AI decisions: knowledge of the work needs a place while the important choices are still open.

item.title: When plans must become care
item.description: For an older person who needs care, municipal plans matter through the help received each day. Norway's audit findings call for closer scrutiny of that connection, alongside the legal duty to provide adequate care and correct shortcomings.

item.title: From farm contracts to school meals: following the money in Cariacica
item.description: School-food records in Cariacica, Brazil, let us follow purchases from family-farm associations through invoices and payments. They reveal part of the journey from farm to school, and point to the people whose experience still needs to be heard.

item.title: Japan’s flexible daycare benefit: finding hours a family can use
item.description: Japan's new benefit gives eligible young children access to limited-hours daycare regardless of whether a parent works. Osaka's application process shows what a family must do before those hours can become part of its week.

item.title: The AI boom can be real. Its financing can still be fragile
item.description: AI may save time at work long before its investors recover the cost of building it. The Bank for International Settlements examines how useful technology and vulnerable financing can grow together.

item.title: Denmark’s greener land plans depend on agreements with owners
item.description: Across Denmark, local groups have mapped possible wetlands, forests and changes to farmland. Making those plans work now means reaching agreements with owners, finding skilled staff and following what happens to the land and water.

item.title: Before, then, if: 25 public experiments worth watching
item.description: A few hours of childcare, a restored wetland, a reliable water supply: public initiatives become interesting when we can see what they might change in daily life. These 25 cases offer concrete starting points for following that work.

item.title: Taiwan is inviting communities to help design the transition
item.description: Local energy, materials that can be used again, and technology shaped around daily life: separate Taiwanese calls invite communities and researchers to help decide what comes next. The opportunities are concrete; the benefits remain to be demonstrated.
